Here, 95% Clopper–Pearson: the range of true rates that the count can't rule out.
How much faster the event (here usually death) happens in one group than another. 1.4 means 40% faster at any moment.

Chance, not the participant or doctor, decides who gets the intervention. The only design here that can show moving a marker causes the outcome.
Using gene variants that raise or lower a marker from birth as a natural experiment: if people born with higher levels don't get more disease, the marker probably isn't the cause.
Methyl groups on DNA, read at CpG sites. Most epigenetic clocks are weighted sums of these.
A place in DNA where a C is followed by a G; the usual site of methylation.
